summary: Standing 40-ft R-6 timber lookout on Confederated Salish and Kootenai land near Arlee, Montana, built 1969 and now staffed only in emergencies.

facts.design: 40-ft treated timber tower with R-6 flat cab; R-6 cabs are a standard 15x15-ft frame house (CSKT)

events.note: NHLR and firelookout.com: 40-ft treated timber tower with R-6 flat cab. CSKT page says built about 1970.
Registered April 12, 2022 as US 1543, MT 106; nominated by Kyle Stetler.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR and firelookout.com say Missoula County; the CSKT lookouts page says Lake County (12 miles east of Arlee). Story reports both. The record's county field is left as the register has it.
NHLR gives 7,636 ft (2,327 m); firelookout.com and the CSKT page give 7,769 ft. Record elevation_m 2327.5 follows the register.
NHLR and firelookout.com say 1969; the CSKT page says about 1970. The story uses 1969.

FFLOS registers a separate Jocko #2 Lookout (US 2089, MT 11), a 1934 60-ft steel tower in Flathead National Forest, removed with only footings left. It is not the NHLR site (US 1543) this record describes.

sources.title: Fire Lookouts
sources.publisher: Confederated Salish and Kootenai Tribes, Division of Fish, Wildlife, Recreation and Conservation

notes_for_editor: Two registrations share the name Jocko #2. This record (NHLR US 1543) is the standing 1969 CSKT R-6 timber tower. FFLOS US 2089 is a different 1934 Forest Service steel tower, removed, with footings only; keep them apart. Access level 'permission' in the record is not supported by any page read; it is left out of facts and should be treated as unverified. County (Missoula vs Lake) and elevation (7,636 vs 7,769 ft) conflict across sources. Staffing comes from an undated CSKT page. Leads not read: nwmt-ffla.org (Northwest Montana Lookout Association, lists historic, staffed and rental lookouts) and the CSKT preservation page. Page-read budget was used up, so no physical-state check was done.
